metaDescription: When to go on a wildlife safari in India, month by month: park seasons, monsoon closures and the best months for tigers, birds, rhinos and snow leopards.
description: A month-by-month guide to the best time for a wildlife safari in India: when parks open and close, why summer is often best for tiger sightings, winter for birds and comfort, the monsoon closure and which parks stay open, and seasons for rhinos, lions, snow leopards and turtles.
dek: The right month can matter as much as the right park. Here is how India's wildlife seasons work, month by month.

about.name: Best time for a wildlife safari in India

intro: Most Indian parks follow the same broad pattern. They open in October or November after the monsoon, stay open through winter and the hot dry months, and close their core zones from about July to September, when rain makes roads impassable and animals breed.
Within that season there is a trade-off. Winter is comfortable and green; summer is hot, but thinner cover and scarce water bring animals into view.
quickAnswer: The best time for a wildlife safari in India is usually between October and June. March to June is often best for tiger sightings, as animals gather at waterholes and cover thins, though it is hot. November to February is cooler and best for birds. Most tiger reserves close core zones from July to September; some buffer zones and a few parks stay open.
takeaways: Most parks are open from October or November to June.
March to June is often best for tiger and mammal sightings.
November to February is best for birds and comfortable weather.
Core zones of most tiger reserves close from about 1 July to 30 September.
Snow leopard trips run from January to March.

sections.heading: Best season by species
list: Tigers: March to June, with October to February for comfort.
Asiatic lions (Gir): December to May; closed 16 June to 15 October.
Rhinos (Kaziranga): November to April, best from February.
Elephants at Kabini: March to June.
Olive ridley nesting in Odisha: about February to April.

sections.heading: What stays open in the monsoon

items.name: Buffer zones
body: Buffer zones of several tiger reserves in Madhya Pradesh, Maharashtra and Rajasthan can run safaris during the monsoon.

items.name: All-year zones
body: In Corbett, Jhirna and Dhela zones are usually open all year; Devalia Safari Park in Gir stays open.

items.name: Western Ghats
body: Parks in Karnataka may run fewer drives but remain open; the forests are at their greenest.

sections.heading: Weighing the trade-offs
paras: If sightings are the priority, go between March and May and plan for heat. If comfort, birds and scenery matter more, go between November and February. Avoid long weekends and holidays if you can, as permits sell out and zones are busier.
after: Our planning guide explains how to book once you have chosen a month.

items.name: Central India
body: Madhya Pradesh and Maharashtra's reserves open in October and close their cores on 30 June. Winter nights are cold; May afternoons can pass 45°C.

items.name: North India
body: Corbett's Dhikala opens in mid-November; Ranthambore and Sariska from October. Winters are cold and foggy in the plains.

items.name: North-east
body: Kaziranga and Manas open in November and close by May, before the floods.

items.name: South India
body: Parks in Karnataka, Kerala and Tamil Nadu often stay open most of the year, with two monsoons affecting them differently.

items.name: The Himalaya
body: Winter for snow leopards; summer (June to September) for high-altitude parks such as the Valley of Flowers.

safety: Carry water and electrolytes in summer.
Dress in layers for winter mornings.
Check closure dates each year; they can change with weather.
No operator can promise a sighting; be wary of anyone who does.
packing: Winter: warm layers, cap and gloves

faqs.q: Which is the best month for a tiger safari?
faqs.a: April and May often give the best sightings, though they are hot. March is a good balance.

faqs.q: Are Indian national parks open in the monsoon?
faqs.a: Most core zones close from about July to September; some buffer zones and a few parks stay open.

faqs.q: When is the best time for birdwatching in India?
faqs.a: November to February, when migrants arrive.

faqs.q: Which parks are open all year?
faqs.a: Corbett's Jhirna and Dhela zones, Devalia in Gir and several parks in south India usually stay open, subject to weather.

faqs.q: Is December good for a safari?
faqs.a: Yes, for comfort and birds, but mornings are very cold and parks are busy during the holidays.

faqs.q: Is October a good time for a safari?
faqs.a: Parks reopen and the forest is green, but thick cover makes sightings harder than in spring.

faqs.q: When do parks reopen after the monsoon?
faqs.a: Usually in October or November; each park announces its own date.
